standard.title: Develop aural and expressive skills
standard.description: develop listening/aural skills and skills for manipulating elements of music to achieve expressive effects when composing, singing and playing instruments
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can manipulate elements during performance and use evaluative listening to compare effects (AC9AMU4D01). They can read from notation and demonstrate developing technique. They have not yet developed the specific aural-skills lens of hearing and adjusting to other parts in real time, or used digital tools systematically for technical development.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students develop listening/aural skills and skills for manipulating elements of music to achieve expressive effects when composing, singing and playing instruments.

nodes.label: Aural skills in ensemble contexts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can listen to other parts when singing or playing in a group and adjust their own volume, tempo or pitch to achieve a balanced ensemble sound.
nodes.minimum_width: Demonstrate one real-time aural adjustment during group performance (e.g. reducing volume when their part is too loud, or adjusting pitch toward the group).
nodes.typical_width: Combine listening and performance skills in ensemble contexts — listening to other parts while playing, adjusting volume for balance, monitoring pitch relative to the group, responding to dynamic signals from conductors or other performers.
wider: Focus on ensemble balance across a full rehearsal — practise listening for specific parts (melody, accompaniment, bass) and adjusting accordingly
Record an ensemble rehearsal, listen back focusing on balance, and identify three specific moments where adjustment improved the sound
nodes.hinge_reason: Aural monitoring during performance — listening and adjusting simultaneously — is the compound skill that distinguishes capable ensemble performers from individual players performing in proximity. Students who cannot do this remain dependent on external feedback from teachers. This is foundational to all ensemble performance work in Y7-8 and beyond.

response_modes.reason: Real-time aural adjustment requires the underlying performance skills to be automatic enough that cognitive bandwidth is available for listening. Build this through repeated ensemble practice with explicit listening focus: 'This rehearsal, focus only on hearing the melody part and matching your dynamic to it.'

success_criteria: Demonstrates at least one real-time aural adjustment during ensemble performance (not prompted by teacher)
Can describe what they heard and what they adjusted in response

nodes.label: Vocal and instrumental techniques for expressive effect
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use vocal or instrumental techniques to manipulate elements of music and create expressive effects — contrast, repetition or balance — in composition and performance.
nodes.minimum_width: Demonstrate at least one technique that creates an expressive effect (e.g. changing timbre to create mood, or using articulation to create contrast) and describe the effect.
nodes.typical_width: Explore vocal and instrumental techniques for creating contrast, repetition and balance — timbre manipulation for mood, articulation techniques, dynamic control, range extension; use focused listening and Viewpoints questions to evaluate effects and set improvement goals; practise and refine techniques for accuracy.
wider: Focus on timbre manipulation: compare how changing tone colour changes mood across different styles — e.g. the same melody played with different articulation, or sung with different vocal quality
Use Viewpoints to analyse how a professional performer achieves a specific expressive effect — develop a practice plan to replicate or adapt that technique

response_modes.reason: Expressive technique development is richer when applied across multiple musical styles and contexts. Each style or context brings different technique priorities — legato playing in classical music differs from staccato articulation in jazz which differs from ornamentation in folk. Breadth of application builds transferable expressive skill.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Developing a personal expressive vocabulary is one of the richest aspects of musical development at Y5-6. Students who explore techniques across multiple styles (classical, contemporary, world music) develop broader expressive options and more musical self-awareness.
success_criteria: Demonstrates at least one vocal or instrumental technique that achieves a described expressive effect
Can explain how the technique creates the effect and how it could be applied in a different musical context

nodes.label: Using digital tools for skill development
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use digital tools (tuner, metronome, recording software) to develop specific technical skills — setting goals, monitoring progress and refining accuracy.
nodes.minimum_width: Use at least one digital tool to monitor a specific technical aspect of their performance (e.g. intonation or tempo accuracy); describe one thing the tool revealed.
nodes.typical_width: Use digital tools systematically for technical development — digital tuner for pitch accuracy, metronome for tempo control, recording software to monitor dynamic range and articulation; set specific technical goals, use tools to track progress, make adjustments.
wider: Use a recording to compare technique before and after a targeted practice period — document what changed and what the digital feedback revealed
Set a specific technical goal (e.g. maintaining consistent dynamics across a full phrase), practise with digital monitoring for two or three sessions, and evaluate progress

response_modes.reason: Digital tools provide feedback that replaces teacher monitoring, but students need to know what to do with the feedback. Build a feedback-action loop: 'The tuner shows you're flat on that note — what will you try to fix it?' The tool's value is in generating data; the skill is in interpreting and acting on it.

success_criteria: Uses at least one digital tool to monitor a specific technical aspect of their performance
Can describe what the tool revealed and one adjustment they made in response
